transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I've called us together to discuss the first-year composition program's proposal to pilot an AI writing-feedback platform in two sections next term. As I understand it, the platform can generate comments on student drafts and can be configured for different levels of instructor control. Before I make a binding decision on whether this pilot may proceed and under what conditions, I'd like to hear from the writing program and the privacy office regarding any instructional or data-handling requirements we should be aware of. Could we start with the writing program's perspective on the proposal?

transcript.text: I should note that the writing program has finalized an adopted pilot standard for this platform. It permits the platform only for formative feedback, requires an instructor to review every generated suggestion before it is released to a student, and prohibits using the platform to assign or determine grades. I finalized this standard this week, but it has not yet been added to the proposal packet.

transcript.text: From the privacy office's perspective, I've completed a vendor review and found that approval requires institutional single sign-on and a signed addendum stating that the vendor retains no student prompts or submissions. The vendor has confirmed it will accept those terms. I should note that my review memo is still awaiting attachment to the proposal packet, but the findings are ready for Dr. Morgan to consider now.
